meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Go on.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, and pasting from another file proves nothing. Show me the history itself, not your summary of it.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And you skipped my question: did you speak to Owen before you entered that zero?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a marking issue, not an offence. And that's twice you haven't told me whether Owen was heard, so I'm taking it as a no.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
He changed his argument in two weeks; that's called thinking. Put both on the desk. You keep handing me paper, Hale, and answering nothing I've said.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him first. A boy cornered by his teacher freezes, and stuck is what paralysis means. Is anything on his record right now?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class against a week at home; of course it's cleaner. I asked you about his record. Yes or no.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then we agree on one thing: 4.3 says a machine's guess establishes nothing on its own. You've walked past his record twice now. Until you say otherwise, I assume something is on it.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

He'll do it, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, away from his class, nothing on file, and I'll want all of that in writing. What's on his record today goes in my email, since you won't say.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
It works. Now when, Hale? His applications close December 1 and that zero is sitting in the gradebook.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12. Your written promise reaches me before he sits down to write it. Ten minutes.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Thursday, November 12, and tonight for the writing. Yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Copies of every document you named today, attached to tonight's email. Nothing else.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Hale
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Today you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, away from his class, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require your written confirmation of those terms, copies of every document you named in the meeting, and a plain answer on whether anything is on his record today. You said I would have this in writing tonight, and it is to reach me before he sits down to write.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record; she still wants your written promise tonight, copies of the documents you named, and an answer on whether anything is on his record now. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.

What moved her: You told her you had spoken to Owen on November 2 and had a note written the same day. That answered the procedural question she walked in with, whether he was heard before the zero, so she had to drop it.

What cost ground: You passed over her question about whether anything is on his record right now, twice. That is the thing she fears most, so she assumed the worst and it is now going to the principal in her email.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the whole essay arriving between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late night in October and the closest your evidence came to it, though nothing said in the meeting ties the two nights together. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she asked whether anything was on his record right now, answer yes or no before bringing out your next document, and answer her objection to the version history before moving on to the quotation.
